root_cause: rich.traceback.Traceback.extract() ignored PEP 678 exception notes (exc.__notes__, Python 3.11+), so the Stack dataclass had no place to hold them and __rich_console__ never rendered them.
best_solution: In Traceback.extract, read notes = getattr(exc_value, '__notes__', None) or [] per exception in the chain and pass the list straight through as a new dataclass field Stack.notes: List[str] = field(default_factory=list) (also added to _SyntaxError). In __rich_console__, after the exc_type/exc_value line, yield one line per note: Text.assemble(('[NOTE] ', 'traceback.note'), highlighter(note)), and register a 'traceback.note' style in default_styles.py. Key point: keep the notes as the original list of strings (mirroring the stdlib attribute), not a joined or str()-ed value.
acceptable_alternatives: Any render format for notes passes; the hidden test only checks the extracted data. Storing the raw __notes__ list (even None when absent, with a wrong Optional[str] annotation) passed, as v4/v6 did. A new style name is optional.
hidden_test_demands: tests/test_traceback.py::test_notes (skipped below 3.11): raise 1/0, call error.add_note('Hello') and add_note('World'), build Traceback() inside the except block, then assert traceback.trace.stacks[0].notes == ['Hello', 'World']. That requires an attribute named exactly `notes` on Stack, holding a list of str in insertion order.
locating_signals: The only signal is 'Exception.__notes__' plus the word 'Notes'. No function is named, but tracebacks in rich live in rich/traceback.py, and grepping for exc_value/Stack( leads to Traceback.extract and the Stack dataclass. The field name `notes` is implied by the dunder name, not stated.
our_outcome_summary: v4 PASS and v6 PASS: both added Stack.notes = getattr(exc_value, '__notes__', None) (annotated Optional[str], but the runtime value is the list) and rendered it after the exception line. v7 FAIL: it wrapped the value as safe_str(notes), so Stack.notes became the string "['Hello', 'World']" and the assert against the list failed (log: assert "['Hello', 'World']" == ['Hello', 'World']). It also referenced a style 'traceback.notes' that was never defined. v8 FAIL: empty patch (35s, 30 calls, 0 chars), so no change was made.
generalizable_lesson: When a statement asks you to 'support' an existing Python attribute (a dunder like __notes__ or __cause__), capture it under the same name without the underscores and keep its native type (list stays list, None becomes an empty default). Don't stringify, join or reformat it on the data model; do formatting only at render time. Hidden tests usually assert on the extracted data structure, not the rendered text. Also check the type annotation you write matches the value (Optional[str] for a list is a sign that stringification will creep in), and never finish with an empty diff.
